The Presidency on Monday said it has begun field operations of the National Agro-Productivity System, its Artificial Intelligence-powered agricultural surveillance platform. This was as it inaugurated the national Project Steering Committee at the State House, Abuja, and deployed 25 trained extension agents across 59 communities in Jigawa State to begin the country’s first real-time, plot-level monitoring of farmland using satellite imagery and machine learning. The Executive Secretary of the Presidential Food Systems Coordinating Unit, Marion Moon, which oversees the system, said the deployment marked a break with decades of post-season data that arrives too late to be actionable. “For too long, decisions about Nigerian agriculture have been made after the season, on figures that arrive too late to act on. NAPS changes that. It gives every tier of government the same timely picture of our farmland, and it is built and owned by Nigerian institutions,” she said. The PFSCU is chaired by Vice President Kashim Shettima and was established after President Bola Tinubu declared a state of emergency on food security in July 2023. The pilot kick-off comes exactly four months after a Federal Government delegation, led by the Deputy Chief of Staff to the President (Office of the Vice President), Ibrahim Hadejia, signed a Memorandum of Understanding in Morocco on July 17 to build the agricultural intelligence capability. According to the committee papers reference, PFSCU/OVP/NAPS/PSC/001, obtained by our correspondent on Monday, “The MoU focuses on technology localisation, dataset calibration, ground-truthing, institutional capacity-building and knowledge transfer. The Vice President’s approval for commencement of the Project’s land availability and utility mapping exercise was conveyed vide Ref: SH/OVP/DCOS/Misc./7174, dated November 26, 2025. “The Vice President designated Jigawa State as the Pilot Implementation State, and His Excellency the President commissioned the NAPS pilot in Dutse, Jigawa State, on 10 November 2026. According to the terms of reference, the Presidency said the extension agents would complete classroom training in Dutse by November 18, after which they would be deployed across Jigawa’s 11 pilot local government areas. It also revealed that the agents would receive coaching from OCP Africa agronomists and begin gathering ground observations to be fed into the AI system to identify and track crops. According to the Director-General of the Jigawa State Agricultural Transformation Agency, Dr Saifullahi Basirka, “NAPS gives Jigawa a clear picture of our farmland and what is happening on it, season by season. This enables us to support farmers where they need it, plan land and water resources with confidence, and demonstrate the real strength of agriculture in Jigawa to investors and lenders.” State police: NASS confirms all 36 assemblies approve bill Tinubu’s education reforms yielding results – Minister Presidency directs release of 78 suspects after convoy attack At the inauguration, Chief Executive Officer of Ground Truth Analysis, Driss Kitane, revealed that NAPS operates by acquiring satellite images of every farm parcel in its coverage area approximately every five days. Machine-learning models automatically classify land cover, delineate individual farm parcels and identify the specific crop on each, without manual mapping, he added. Field agents on the ground will collect validation observations using Ground Truth Analytics’ data-collection application, which continuously calibrates and improves the accuracy of the models in a process known as ground-truthing. OCP Africa’s Head of Digital, Akintunde Akinwade, one of the system’s technical partners, said the platform was designed to answer the questions of who is farming a given plot, what they are planting, where it is located, and when, through continuous tracking of crop growth stages across the entire season. “When you map parcels to the owners of the parcels, you know the who. We know the crop that is planted. We know the location. And we know the phenological growth stage of the farming across the entire season,” he said. According to him, the Phase 1 pilot focuses on rice, wheat and maize cultivation across 59 communities spanning 11 of Jigawa’s 27 local government areas, covering the four agricultural zones of the state. The pilot runs over the 2026/2027 dry season from November 2026 to April 2027, aiming to mobilise field agents in month one, deliver a baseline land-cover map of Jigawa in month two, produce first crop maps, and commence five-day monitoring from approximately January 2027. Other deliverables include yield data collection and a validation report in month five, and delivery of the full platform and Phase 1 report to the Steering Committee in the sixth month. At its inaugural meeting on Monday, the steering committee also selected two additional states for high-level land-cover mapping, with its next milestone set for January 31, 2027. The committee includes representatives from the Ministries of Agriculture and Food Security, Water Resources and Sanitation, the National Space Research and Development Agency and the Nigeria Governors’ Forum, alongside six states representing the geopolitical zones. They include Jigawa (North-West and pilot state), Borno (North-East), Plateau (North-Central), Ekiti (South-West), Ebonyi (South-East) and Cross River (South-South). GTA and OCP Africa participate as technical and operational partners.
